pages.text:
Oluhle wakes up early.
She is excited to get water.

“Come Mama, we have to be first
today,” she calls.
pages.action: reaches up for her pink bucket and hurries Mama
pages.change: Oluhle wakes early, eager to be first at the communal tap with Mama
pages.question_created: Will they be first at the tap?

notes: kitchen in pale blue; Oluhle seen from behind stretching up; Mama smiling
illustration.only_in_image: Oluhle's bucket is a small pink one kept on a high kitchen shelf she has to stretch for; Mama already holds a yellow bucket and a cloth.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
On the way they meet
Nathi and Unathi.
They are going to the tap
with their mother.
pages.action: the children skip and run ahead together
pages.change: Friends Nathi and Unathi join the walk to the tap

notes: three children seen mostly from behind, running
illustration.only_in_image: Only the three children are drawn, skipping and running on a green slope; the grown-ups the text mentions are out of the frame.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
Oluhle and her friends play while
the grown-ups get water.

“Oluhle, your bucket is full,”
says Mama.
pages.action: the children play while the adults fill buckets
pages.change: Oluhle's bucket is filled; the morning trip is done

notes: still life of bucket and standpipe
illustration.only_in_image: The picture shows no people at all: only the pink bucket standing beside a tall yellow standpipe, so the tap itself is introduced by the picture.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
At home, Oluhle takes a bath.
Mama goes to work and Oluhle
stays with Makhulu.
pages.action: Oluhle bathes in a tub; Mama leaves for work
pages.change: Mama goes to work and Oluhle is left with her grandmother

notes: bath is a yellow tub on the floor; Oluhle smiles
illustration.only_in_image: The pink bucket stands on top of a chest of drawers behind the bath, the last time it is shown in a place at home; Mama is drawn only from the waist down, leaving with a pink handbag.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
In the afternoon Makhulu
starts to make supper.
She needs more water.
She calls Oluhle so they
can go to the tap.
pages.action: Makhulu starts supper and finds she needs more water
pages.change: A second trip to the tap becomes necessary
pages.question_created: Will they go to the tap again?

notes: grandmother in a pink spotted headwrap and dress; yellow bucket at the edge
illustration.only_in_image: Makhulu is drawn startled, mouth open and with small alarm strokes beside her head, over an empty pot; the text states the need calmly.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
“Makhulu, I can’t find my bucket.
I searched everywhere,”
says Oluhle.

Makhulu helps her look, but the
bucket is nowhere to be found.
pages.action: Oluhle and Makhulu search for the missing bucket
pages.change: Oluhle's bucket is missing and a search does not find it
pages.question_created: Where is the bucket, and how will she carry water now?
pages.page_turn_note: Strongest turn: the search fails and the reader wants to know how Oluhle will carry water.

notes: close-up head on a pale blue shape; small pink bucket cut off at the page corner
illustration.only_in_image: A single tear runs down Oluhle's cheek in a close-up of her face; outside the scene frame, the lost pink bucket peeks into the lower-left corner of the page.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Makhulu thinks of a plan.
She gets a 2-litre bottle from
the cupboard and fetches
paints and paint brushes.
pages.action: Makhulu fetches a plastic bottle, paints and brushes
pages.change: Makhulu has a plan instead of a bucket
pages.question_created: What will she make with a bottle and paint?

notes: still life: jug centred, paint tubes and brushes around it on green
illustration.only_in_image: The 'bottle' is drawn as a large plastic jug with a handle; the lost pink bucket now tumbles in at the top margin.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
Makhulu makes a bucket from
the water bottle.
She paints it pink.
“Here’s a recycled bucket, Oluhle!”
pages.action: Makhulu cuts the jug into a bucket, paints it pink and gives it to Oluhle
pages.change: Oluhle has a new, home-made pink bucket

notes: the lost bucket drifts at the bottom margin
illustration.only_in_image: The new bucket carries painted white flowers and a yellow handle, details the text does not mention; it is shown held up in two hands with no face, so the giver's pride is left to the reader.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“Thank you, Makhulu,” says Oluhle.
She is excited to go to the tap with
her new recycled bucket.
pages.change: Oluhle's sadness turns into excitement for the next trip

notes: lost bucket at the left edge
illustration.only_in_image: The close-up repeats the tearful face of page 6 in the same framing, now with a gap-toothed grin and bright cheeks, so the change is read by comparing two faces.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
The next day Unathi and Nathi
bring two bottles to Makhulu.

“Makhulu, could you please make
recycled buckets for us?”
pages.action: Unathi and Nathi bring two bottles and ask for buckets of their own
pages.change: The idea spreads: the friends want recycled buckets too

notes: lost bucket at the bottom margin
illustration.only_in_image: The two children are drawn waving and holding up large empty jugs, seen from slightly above.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
Makhulu paints their buckets
yellow and blue, their
favourite colours.
Nathi and Unathi are happy.
Oluhle is happy too.
pages.action: Makhulu paints the friends' jugs yellow and blue
pages.change: Everyone has a bucket and all three children are happy

notes: still life of yellow and teal jugs with brushes; repeats the composition of page 7

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
The friends can’t wait to show off
with their new buckets.

“Can we go to the tap now?”
they ask.
pages.action: The friends line up their new buckets and ask to go to the tap
pages.change: The friends are ready to show off their buckets on the way to the tap
pages.question_created: Can they go to the tap now?
pages.page_turn_note: Last story page ends on the children's question; the trip itself is never shown. The turn leads only to the closing vignette of the lost bucket.

notes: three buckets in a row in front of the three children; the following unnumbered vignette shows the lost bucket alone on white
illustration.only_in_image: Each finished bucket has its own painted pattern (flowers, triangles, squares) and the handles are in each other's colours; one boy covers his mouth with both hands as if giggling; the lost bucket sits again in the lower-left corner.

pages.label: OBSERVED
